title: Spotify — Web/App Homepage
creator: Spotify AB
observed_layout: Dark theme base, large full-bleed editorial hero imagery, card-based content rows with horizontal scroll
visual_hierarchy: Imagery and bold headline drive hierarchy over UI chrome; navigation stays minimal and recedes
typography_character: Bold, condensed sans-serif for headlines; high contrast against dark background
spacing_character: Generous section spacing, dense card rows within sections
color_character: Near-black base, single accent color (green) used sparingly for CTA/active/playing state only
interaction_pattern: Hover-reveal play controls on cards, persistent bottom player bar
useful_principle: Dark base + single restrained accent color is exactly the Night Stage color discipline (Cyan instead of green), and imagery/typography (not chrome) carries brand energy.
do_not_copy: Spotify's specific green accent, exact card proportions, and its persistent global player bar (not part of TJ MEDIA's scope)
notes: Category A (Hero/Music Brand). Apply to Main Hero dark section only, not site-wide.

title: Shazam — Brand/App Design Language
creator: Apple Inc. (Shazam)
observed_layout: Dark gradient background with a central pulsing/listening animation as the sole hero focal point
visual_hierarchy: One dominant animated graphic communicates the entire brand action (listening); text is minimal
typography_character: Minimal, large, short headline text; typography plays a supporting role only
spacing_character: Very open, uncluttered around the central graphic
color_character: Dark base with a glowing radial accent (blue/purple gradient) concentrated at the center
interaction_pattern: Single primary action (tap to listen), pulse animation implies real-time activity
useful_principle: Radial 'Spotlight' glow concentrated on one focal point (search action) — directly maps to TJ MEDIA's Hero SearchBar as the energy focal point.
do_not_copy: Shazam's specific gradient hue, the literal pulse/listening animation concept (TJ MEDIA is not an audio-recognition product), full-screen single-purpose layout
notes: Category A (Hero/Music Brand). Apply concentrated spotlight glow behind Hero SearchBar only.

title: Apple Music — Browse/Editorial Pages
creator: Apple Inc.
observed_layout: Large-format square artwork tiles in generous grids, minimal text overlay, editorial curation rows
visual_hierarchy: Artwork itself is the primary hierarchy driver; UI chrome is nearly invisible
typography_character: Light-weight, small metadata text beneath large artwork; typography never competes with imagery
spacing_character: Wide gutters between tiles, artwork given maximum visual weight
color_character: Light/white base by default; color comes from the artwork itself, not UI paint
interaction_pattern: Tap artwork to play/preview; horizontal scroll rows for browsing
useful_principle: Artwork-forward grid where a single consistent artwork system (not literal photos) can still visually anchor a discovery page — directly applicable to Latest Songs.
do_not_copy: Apple's use of real licensed album artwork (TJ MEDIA must use a generated Artwork System, never real album covers per project_asset_restrictions)
notes: Category B (Artwork/Music Discovery). Apply grid rhythm and generous artwork sizing to Latest Songs; artwork content itself must be the generated system, not real covers.

title: SoundCloud — Track Page / Waveform Player
creator: SoundCloud Global Ltd.
observed_layout: Waveform visualization stretched horizontally as the primary player surface, artwork placed alongside as a secondary element
visual_hierarchy: The waveform itself is the dominant visual element, not the artwork or metadata
typography_character: Compact metadata (title/artist/play count) below the waveform, secondary in weight
spacing_character: Full-width waveform with minimal surrounding padding
color_character: Waveform rendered in a single bright accent color against a neutral track background
interaction_pattern: Scrub/seek directly on the waveform; comment markers overlaid on the waveform timeline
useful_principle: Waveform-as-primary-visual-element is the clearest real-world precedent for TJ MEDIA's 'Waveform/Equalizer' motif — confirms it reads as a legitimate music-product visual language, not decoration.
do_not_copy: SoundCloud's literal scrubbable/interactive waveform player mechanic and its specific orange color (TJ MEDIA keeps Cyan)
notes: Category B (Artwork/Music Discovery). Confirms Waveform motif legitimacy for Hero/Section Accent use; do not build an interactive scrubber.

title: Billboard Hot 100 Chart
creator: Billboard/Penske Media Corporation
observed_layout: Dense vertical ranking table/list, large rank number at the far left of each row, small artwork thumbnail, title/artist, and a rank-change indicator
visual_hierarchy: Rank number is the single largest visual element per row, larger than song title or artwork
typography_character: Heavy, oversized numerals for rank; smaller regular weight for song/artist text
spacing_character: Compact row height to maximize how many ranked items are visible at once
color_character: Neutral base with small colored arrows/badges (up/down/new) as the only accent color use
interaction_pattern: Static ranked list, occasional filter by chart type/date
useful_principle: Oversized rank numerals as the dominant visual element, plus a minimal color-coded rank-change indicator — this is the exact 'Large Ranking Number + Ranking Change' language for TJ MEDIA's Music Chart page.
do_not_copy: Billboard's specific editorial branding, ad placements, and multi-chart tabbed navigation complexity beyond TJ MEDIA's 3-tab scope (TOP100/HOT100/올해 인기곡)
notes: Category C (Chart/Ranking/Music Data). Primary reference for Music Chart page ranking row structure.

title: Beatport — Top 100 / Genre Charts
creator: Beatport LLC
observed_layout: Dark, data-dense chart table with small artwork, genre tabs above the list, and a waveform preview that appears on row hover
visual_hierarchy: Data density is prioritized over whitespace; many rows visible per screen, typography carries most of the identity
typography_character: Compact, functional typography optimized for scanning many rows quickly
spacing_character: Tight row spacing, tabs and filters compressed into a single control bar
color_character: Dark background with a single bright accent for active tab/hover state
useful_principle: Combines a Dark data-dense chart surface with tab-based filtering — validates pairing 'Night Stage' Dark Section with 'Data Rhythm' dense ranking rows on the same Chart page.
do_not_copy: Beatport's hover-audio-preview interaction (out of scope) and DJ-specific metadata (BPM/Key) irrelevant to TJ MEDIA's karaoke context
notes: Category C (Chart/Ranking/Music Data). Confirms Dark theme is appropriate specifically for the Chart page, supporting the 70/30 blend.

title: Genius — Song/Lyrics Page
creator: Genius Media Group
observed_layout: Oversized song title as the page's dominant element, artwork positioned as a secondary supporting block, generous line-height body text
visual_hierarchy: Typography (song title) outranks imagery in visual weight, unusual among music sites
typography_character: Very large, bold display type for titles; comfortable reading line-height for lyrics/body text
spacing_character: Wide vertical rhythm between title block and content sections
color_character: Light neutral base, minimal color accents reserved for highlighted lyric annotations
interaction_pattern: Click-to-annotate on lyric lines (not applicable to TJ MEDIA)
useful_principle: Typography-first hierarchy (large title dominating over artwork) is a useful alternate pattern for Song Detail's information-heavy sections (Genre/Registration/Release Info).
do_not_copy: Genius's annotation/community-comment interaction model entirely out of scope
notes: Category D (Typography/Layout). Apply large-title-first hierarchy to Song Detail's info block, not as a full-page pattern.

title: Bandcamp — Artist/Release Grid
creator: Bandcamp, Inc. (Epic Games)
observed_layout: Simple square artwork grid with minimal chrome, clean typographic labels beneath each tile
visual_hierarchy: Balanced — artwork and typography share weight equally, neither dominates
typography_character: Plain, functional sans-serif, no decorative styling
color_character: Mostly neutral/white base, color comes entirely from artwork tiles
interaction_pattern: Simple hover state, click-through to release page
useful_principle: A restrained, low-chrome artwork grid confirms that Latest Songs does not need heavy decoration — the generated Artwork System itself can carry visual interest within a simple neutral grid.
notes: Category D (Typography/Layout). Supports keeping Latest Songs grid itself simple/neutral, consistent with the Design Rule that heavy motifs stay confined to Hero/Chart.
